rows.Enduring Risk: Pricing, affordability, access and competitive pressures
rows.Risk Statement:
The pricing and market access environment is
highly complex and subject to dynamic economic,
political and social pressures. Deterioration in
socio-economic conditions may affect customers’
ability or willingness to purchase our medicines
and may adversely affect our business and
results of operations.
rows.Current Year Update:
At AstraZeneca, our approach to pricing balances the priorities of patients, their
physicians, payers, society and our business. Our four guiding principles – Access,
Value, Sustainability and Equity – aligned to our overarching Company Values,
form the cornerstones of our brand pricing strategies. Our prices are rooted in the
assurance of our high-quality science, and the benefit this brings to patients. They
also reflect holistic value, in the context of healthcare systems and market dynamics,
affordability and equity; so that we can adapt our prices across the more than
80 countries in which we have an active presence and help support long-term
healthcare system resilience.
Our pricing approach, as described in the previous paragraph, is a key contributor
to our success. However, there are various external risk factors that could
compromise our ability to execute our pricing strategies as planned. The market
access environment is highly complex and subject to dynamic economic, political
and social pressures. Globally, there are increasing cost-containment measures,
greater calls for net price and R&D cost transparency, as well as early discussions
towards pooled procurement mechanisms beyond emergency countermeasures
and essential medicines.
Continued deterioration of, or lack of improvement in, socio-
economic conditions could adversely affect supply and/or
distribution in affected countries and the ability or willingness of
customers to purchase our medicines, putting pressure on price
and/or volumes. This could adversely affect our business or results
of operations, for example, those healthcare systems most severely
impacted by downturn may seek alternative ways to settle their
debts at a discount. Other customers may cease to trade, which may
result in losses from writing off debts or a reduction in demand for
products. Across the industry, we continue to navigate pricing
pressures and policy changes including the EU Joint Clinical
Assessment (JCA), the US Inflation Reduction Act (IRA) as well
as more recent health equalisation initiatives requiring countries to
increase their drug spending to support R&D costs, ensuring a more
balanced global pharmaceutical landscape.

Material Controls.Name: Pricing policy approval by SET
Material Controls.Description:
WHAT & WHY
SET price guidance sets the methods and practical considerations to support implementation of the pricing policy, such that approved pricing policies ensure that prices charged for products are appropriate to give value to patients and HCP, are not seen as anti-competitive and are in line with business case.  Any exceptions to the agreed policy are subject to appropriate approvals.
 
 
HOW
The Pricing and Market Access Director for each brand works with Global Price implementation team (and others) to develop a pricing policy that is in line with the guidance approved and issued by SET.  Price policy is periodically reviewed (usually every 2 years - it can be updated ad hoc) and re-approved as required.  Policy includes target and floor prices (set for each of the 3 access tiers).  Price approvals are submitted by Marketing companies into the PRICE tool and if above floor can be approved by Area VP.   All prices that go beyond boundary of pricing policy require (BU) EVP approval.
 
WHEN
Event driven (new product launches, changing environment, out of thresholds) or periodic review

Material Controls.Name: Products to Patients Pipeline Governance
Material Controls.Description:
WHAT & WHY
A rigorous stage gate process that ensures that new medicines being developed are safe, effective, affordable, profitable and aligned with the Business strategy.  The process also ensures that scarce company resources are being put to the best possible use.

HOW
The AstraZeneca “Products to Patients” (P2P) operating model is a series of structured reviews and approval gates for pipeline assets in development.  Global Project Teams (GPTs) bring comprehensive business cases / progress updates to the Early-Stage Product Committee (ESPC) and / or Late-Stage Product Committee (LSPC), which are governance advisory bodies that review, debate, endorse and make recommendations for approval of decisions by the IPCo Board(s) (Company Boards of the Intellectual Property-owning legal entities).

The ESPC/LSPC provide consistent, rigorous, and multi-disciplinary assessments of potential investments, including new opportunities, with a focus on risk, time, cost and value.  The committees also review components of TA strategy (e.g. molecule combination strategies, disease area strategies, end-to-end life-cycle management strategies for key brands) as an extension of the annual Therapeutic Area (TA) Strategy review, which is approved by SET.   Through this governance advisory body, AstraZeneca aims to balance portfolio risk across the therapeutic areas.  

ESPC is jointly chaired by the R&D EVPs for each TA unit.  LSPC is chaired by the Chief Executive Officer.  All committee include members of SET and SET-1 leaders.

WHEN
Event driven by pipeline progression timetables

rows.Current Year Update:

of our strategy and the delivery of our short- and medium-term targets. We may
ultimately be unable to achieve commercial success for various reasons, including:
Failure to execute our commercial strategies or achieve the level
of sales anticipated for a medicine could materially impact our
business.
-Difficulties in manufacturing sufficient quantities of the product
-Any price control measures imposed by governments and healthcare authorities
-Patient access to healthcare
Failure to leverage potential opportunities or appropriately manage
risks in emerging markets may materially adversely affect our
reputation, business or results of operations.
-Diagnosis rates
-Erosion of IP rights
-Failure to show a differentiated product profile
-Changes in prescribing habits.
The ability to successfully carry out business in emerging markets can be
more challenging than in established markets. Such challenges may include:
-Volatility in economic or political climates
-Inadequate protection against crime (including counterfeiting,
corruption and fraud)
-Inadvertent breaches of local and international law.
Failure to execute our commercial strategies or achieve the level
of sales anticipated for a medicine could materially impact our
business.
Failure to leverage potential opportunities or appropriately manage
risks in emerging markets may materially adversely affect our
reputation, business or results of operations.

Material Controls.Name: 10yr Long-Range Plan (LRP)
Material Controls.Description:
WHAT & WHY
The Long-Term Plan (LTP) is the annual 10-year financial plan, agreed with the CEO and CFO and approved by the Board in July.  It serves as the plan of record for the current year; supports balance sheet and intangible asset calculations; supports the Company’s long-term ambition on revenue and growth.
 
HOW
The LTP integrates TA Strategy and long-term forecasting into a single 10-year financial plan. The TA Strategy process that underpins the LTP is developed collaboratively by Commercial, R&D, Finance, and GPPM teams across the Therapeutic Areas and central functions.  The first four years of the LTP are effectively superseded by the Mid-Term Plan (MTP), which operationalises the LTP and informs the following year’s budget-setting process. In this way, the LTP helps aligns medium- and short-term plans to long-term targets.
 
WHEN
Annually in June and approved by the Board in July.

In addition, periodic in-year financial reforecasts are performed as part of our annual planning cycle; with updates presented against the agreed Budget baseline, allowing changes to be made and implemented (as required).
 
HOW
The SET receive monthly Performance Reports from the Group Business Performance team, incorporating YTD performance against Budget and latest financial reforecasts (as relevant) along with progress against our Global Scorecard KPIs. 
Financial reforecasts are presented and discussed with the SET on a periodic basis, as part of the annual planning cycle.   

WHEN
Internal SET Performance Reports are distributed on a monthly basis. 
Financial reforecasts are performed on a periodic basis as part of the annual planning cycle.

HOW

WHEN

rows.Enduring Risk: Failure to meet regulatory & ethical expectations on commercial practices, including anti-bribery and corruption, and scientific exchanges
rows.Risk Statement: Any failure to comply with applicable laws, rules and regulations, including anti-bribery/anti-corruption and anti-fraud legislation, may result in civil and/or criminal legal proceedings and/or regulatory sanctions, fines or penalties, impacting financial results.
rows.Current Year Update:
There remains an increased global focus on the implementation and enforcement
of anti-bribery/anti-corruption and anti-fraud legislation. Three relevant pieces
of legislation include the UK Bribery Act, the UK Economic Crime and Corporate
Transparency Act and the US Foreign Corrupt Practices Act. Many other countries
where we operate are also enforcing their own laws more aggressively and/or
adopting tougher new measures. There has also been an increase in cooperation
and coordination between regulators across countries with respect to investigation
and enforcement. We have been the subject of anti-corruption investigations and
there can be no assurance that we will not, from time to time, be subject to informal
enquiries and formal investigations from governmental agencies. In the context
of our business, governmental officials interact with us in various roles that are
important to our operations, such as in the capacity of a regulator, partner or
healthcare payer, reimburser or prescriber, among others. To the extent we are the
subject of any such pending and material matters, details are included in Note 30
to the Financial Statements from page 181 of AstraZeneca’s Annual Report and
Form 20-F Information 2025.
Despite taking measures to prevent breaches of applicable
anti-bribery/anti-corruption and anti-fraud laws by our personnel
and associated third parties, breaches may still occur, potentially
resulting in the imposition of significant penalties, such as fines, the
requirement to comply with monitoring or self-reporting obligations,
or debarment or exclusion from government sales or reimbursement
programmes, any of which could materially adversely affect our
reputation, business or results of operations.

- review the Company’s procedures for detecting fraud                                                                                                                      
- Review of the scope for compliance effectiveness reviews and review of the resources for, the role, effectiveness, structure and organisation of the compliance function.  (IRM:  CTRL0032451 and CTRL0032454)

Annual cycle of reporting

rows.Enduring Risk: Failure or delay in the delivery of our pipeline or launch of new medicines
rows.Risk Statement: The development of pharmaceutical product candidates is a complex, risky and lengthy process involving significant resources. A project may fail at any stage of the process due to a number of factors, which could adversely affect our future business and results of operations.
rows.Current Year Update:
Our continued success depends on the development and successful launch
of innovative new drugs.
The development of pharmaceutical product candidates is a complex, risky and
lengthy process involving significant resources. Projects have failed, and may fail
in the future, at any stage of the process due to various factors, including: failure to
obtain the required regulatory or marketing approvals, unfavourable clinical efficacy
data, safety concerns, failure to demonstrate adequate cost-effective benefits to
regulatory authorities and/or payers, and the emergence of competing products.
Launch activities have been delayed, and may be delayed in the future, by a number
of factors, including: adverse findings in preclinical or clinical studies, regulatory
demands, price negotiation, large-scale natural disasters or global pandemics,
competitor activity and technology transfer.
In addition to developing products in-house, we continue to expand our portfolio
through licensing arrangements and strategic collaborations which may not
ultimately be successful.
Failure or delay in development of new product candidates could
damage the reputation of our R&D capabilities, and adversely affect
our future business and results of operations.
Delays to launches can lead to excess expenses in the manufacture
of pre-launch inventories, marketing materials and salesforce
training. For the launch of products that are seasonal in nature,
delays in regulatory approvals or manufacturing may delay launch
to the next season which, in turn, may significantly reduce the
return on costs incurred in preparing for the launch for that season.
Furthermore, in immuno-oncology in particular, speed to market
is critical given the large number of clinical trials being conducted
by competitors. Delay of launch can also erode the term of
patent exclusivity.
Competition from other pharmaceutical companies means that we
may have to pay a significant premium over book or market values
for our acquisitions. Failure to complete collaborative projects in a
timely, cost-effective manner may limit our ability to access a greater
portfolio of products, intellectual property (IP), technology and
shared expertise. In many cases, we make milestone payments in
advance of the commercialisation of the products, with no assurance
of recouping costs.

rows.Enduring Risk: Safety & efficacy of marketed medicines is questioned
rows.Risk Statement: Safety concerns relating to our products may lead to recalls, seizures, interruption of supply and loss of product approvals, which could adversely affect patient access, our reputation and our revenues. Significant product liability claims could also arise, which may be costly, divert management attention, reduce demand for our products and damage our reputation.
rows.Current Year Update:
Our ability to accurately assess, prior to launch, the eventual safety or efficacy of a
new product once in broader clinical use can only be based on data available at that
time, which is inherently limited due to relatively short periods of product testing
and relatively small clinical study patient samples.
Any unforeseen safety concerns or adverse events relating to our products, or failure
to comply with laws, rules and regulations relating to provision of appropriate
warnings concerning the dangers and risks of our products that result in injuries,
could expose us to large product liability claims, settlements and awards, particularly
in the US. Adverse publicity relating to the safety of a product, or of other competing
products, may increase the risk of product liability claims.
Serious safety concerns or adverse events relating to our products
could lead to product recalls, seizures, loss of product approvals,
declining sales and interruption of supply, and could materially
adversely impact patient access, our reputation and financial
revenues. Significant product liability claims could also arise which
could be costly, divert management attention, or damage our
reputation and demand for our products.
Unfavourable resolution of such current and similar future product
liability claims could subject us to enhanced damages, consumer
fraud and/or other claims, including civil and criminal governmental
actions. This could require us to make significant provisions in our
accounts relating to legal proceedings and could materially
adversely affect our financial condition or results of operations,
particularly where such circumstances are not covered by insurance.

Material Controls.Name: Executive Safety Board
Material Controls.Description:
WHAT & WHY
The Executive Safety Board (ESB) is the highest level of safety governance at AstraZeneca for patient and product safety matters. The ESB makes decisions related to the following topics, when a company position/strategy is required:
• Safety of patients who receive treatment with AstraZeneca products
• Any safety risk, concern or finding that impacts the benefit/risk profile of an AstraZeneca product(s)

The Executive Safety Board will be automatically triggered for important emerging safety concerns/issues that impact the benefit risk profile of an AstraZeneca product including but not limited to a product in development (investigational product) or a product being used in post marketed setting.

HOW
ESB topics are to include important emerging safety concern(s), or safety advice seeking matters, related to an investigational or a marketed product:
• Review and evaluation of the impact of significant new toxicology or safety findings that could affect the benefit-risk profile of a product and/or the continuation and dosing of clinical studies or the withdrawal of a product from the market. This includes unexpected serious safety matters identified by a Data Monitoring Committee (DMC). 
• Proposal for re-entry of a product into clinical development when safety was a factor leading to its discontinuation and approve the decision to continue dosing in a study where dosing had been previously discontinued due to safety concerns.
• Proposal for re-starting dosing in a study and/or clinical program when safety was a factor leading to its clinical hold and/or decision to discontinue enrolment/dosing.
• Guidance on complex safety matters related, including those related to product labelling.
• As per SOP MANAGEMENT OF IMPORTANT NEW SAFETY ISSUES (SOP-0108734, V3)

If a decision cannot be reached by the PS TA VP and QPPV, the issue can be escalated to the ESB for final resolution. The QPPV also has single authority to escalate the matter to ESB (see QPPV SOP). The SSaMT members, SPVMD and TPL (for non-clinical INSIs) should be included in any discussion relating to the dispute. Due to the potential impact on the overall benefit/risk of the product and public health, dispute resolution discussions must occur with the utmost urgency following initial awareness of the safety signal. If resolution cannot be reached within an appropriate timeframe and without undue delay, the default position is to proceed with reporting.

· PS TA VP can raise a topic for ESB on an ad-hoc basis.

The ESB should be informed of endorsements for recommendations made in the management of an INSI (for clinical and non-clinical topics). When a joint decision has not been reached between PS TA VP and clinical development VP or PS TA VP wants to specially escalate ESB for ESB review

WHEN
Event driven due to emerging safety concerns/issues

rows.Enduring Risk: Failure to meet regulatory or ethical requirements for medicine development or approval
rows.Risk Statement: We are subject to laws and regulations that control our ability to market our pharmaceutical products. Delays in regulatory approvals could delay our ability to market our products and may adversely affect our revenue.
rows.Current Year Update:
We are subject to laws and regulations that control our ability to market our
pharmaceutical products. Our development programmes must meet many standards
to prove our products are safe, effective and of high quality. Health authorities, such
as the FDA in the US and the European Medicines Agency in the EU, can refuse to
approve our products or require us to conduct additional clinical trials or scientific
testing before they will approve them for marketing. Many factors influence health
authority decisions to approve or reject a marketing application for a pharmaceutical
product. These include advances in science and technology, new laws, regulations
and policies, and different standards for evaluating safety and effectiveness.
Delays in regulatory approvals could delay our ability to market our
products and may adversely affect our revenue. Also, post-approval
requirements, including additional clinical trials, could cause
increased costs. We seek to manage these risks, but policymaking
by governments and health authorities can be unpredictable and
unforeseen circumstances, such as public health emergencies,
may strain health authority resources and delay the approval of
our products.
Following approval, a health authority may require us to conduct
additional clinical trials or scientific testing to address concerns
raised after patients have used our products in the marketplace.
New data may impact a product’s approval status or lead to labelling
changes that limit the use of a product.

Material Controls.Description:
WHAT & WHY
A rigorous stage gate process that ensures that new medicines being developed are safe, effective, affordable, profitable and aligned with the Business strategy.  The process also ensures that scarce company resources are being put to the best possible use.

HOW
The AstraZeneca “Products to Patients” (P2P) operating model is a series of structured reviews and approval gates for pipeline assets in development.  Global Project Teams (GPTs) bring comprehensive business cases / progress updates to the Early-Stage Product Committee (ESPC) and / or Late-Stage Product Committee (LSPC), which are governance advisory bodies that review, debate, endorse and make recommendations for approval of decisions by the IPCo Board(s) (Company Boards of the Intellectual Property-owning legal entities).

The ESPC/LSPC provide consistent, rigorous, and multi-disciplinary assessments of potential investments, including new opportunities, with a focus on risk, time, cost and value.  The committees also review components of TA strategy (e.g. molecule combination strategies, disease area strategies, end-to-end life-cycle management strategies for key brands) as an extension of the annual Therapeutic Area (TA) Strategy review, which is approved by SET.   Through this governance advisory body, AstraZeneca aims to balance portfolio risk across the therapeutic areas.  

ESPC is jointly chaired by the R&D EVPs for each TA unit.  LSPC is chaired by the Chief Executive Officer.  All committee include members of SET and SET-1 leaders.

WHEN
Event driven by pipeline progression timetables

rows.Enduring Risk: Failure to maintain supply of compliant, quality medicines
rows.Risk Statement: Supply chain difficulties may result in product shortages which could lead to lost product sales and materially affect our reputation and results of operations.
rows.Risk Category: Supply chain and business execution risks
rows.Current Year Update:
During Q1 2026, the risk of supply chain disruption resulting in product shortages remains elevated but stable, reflecting continued exposure to external geopolitical volatility, trade controls, and operational complexity across the global supply network. Key drivers include heightened geopolitical tensions and sanctions regimes affecting certain markets, ongoing dependency on a limited number of critical suppliers, and increased operational strain as demand patterns evolve across regions.
Risk updates from Global Functions, International Commercial and Procurement indicate that while no material widespread shortages have crystallised in the quarter, the environment remains fragile, with a low tolerance for execution failures. The potential for supply disruption continues to present a direct reputational risk, particularly where continuity of medicine supply is critical to patients and regulators, and a financial risk through lost sales or delayed revenue recognition if disruptions are not proactively managed.
Encouragingly, mitigation maturity has improved in several areas, including enhanced supplier risk visibility, inventory management actions, and more structured stress‑testing of supply scenarios. However, the residual risk remains driven by external dependencies and the increasing complexity of the end‑to‑end supply chain, requiring sustained senior management oversight and continued investment in resilience capabilities.

Material Controls.Name: 10yr Long-Range Plan (LRP)
Material Controls.Description:
WHAT & WHY
The Long-Term Plan (LTP) is the annual 10-year financial plan, agreed with the CEO and CFO and approved by the Board in July.  It serves as the plan of record for the current year; supports balance sheet and intangible asset calculations; supports the Company’s long-term ambition on revenue and growth.
 
HOW
The LTP integrates TA Strategy and long-term forecasting into a single 10-year financial plan. The TA Strategy process that underpins the LTP is developed collaboratively by Commercial, R&D, Finance, and GPPM teams across the Therapeutic Areas and central functions.  The first four years of the LTP are effectively superseded by the Mid-Term Plan (MTP), which operationalises the LTP and informs the following year’s budget-setting process. In this way, the LTP helps aligns medium- and short-term plans to long-term targets.
 
WHEN
Annually in June and approved by the Board in July.

In addition, Annually a QMS Regulatory Compliance Status report is prepared.  The report summarises the status of the QMS and GxP compliance, including findings from internal and external inspections. The report is approved by the SVP Global Quality and VP R&D Quality Assurance and is shared with the Board.

rows.Enduring Risk: Failure in Information technology or cyber security
rows.Risk Statement: Significant disruption to our IT systems, including cybersecurity breaches, or failure to comply with applicable laws or regulations could harm our reputation and materially affect our financial condition or results of operations.
rows.Risk Category: Supply chain and business execution risks
rows.Current Year Update:
IT systems enable critical business functions which are increasingly dependent on
solution provider cybersecurity controls and maturity. High availability and resilient
IT systems remain a business imperative, providing our workforce with continuous
access to AI tools, collaboration environments, global communications channels,
applications and data. In addition to availability and reliability, these systems must
comply with provisions specified in cybersecurity, data security, privacy and
individual protection laws.
We prioritise data protection and access to delivery innovation, business growth,
and uninterrupted medicine supply. Data is often characterised as strictly
confidential including clinical trial records, personal information, IP, R&D data, and
compliance information. IT systems and data are potentially vulnerable to service
interruptions and security breaches via attacks by malicious third parties or
intentional or inadvertent actions by our employees or vendors. Attempts to exploit
AstraZeneca’s IT systems and data are increasingly sophisticated with increased
volume and fuelled by malicious AI use. Threat actors include organised criminal
groups, ‘hacktivists’, nation states, employees and others. Privacy legislation
includes obligations to report data protection breaches to regulators and affected
individuals within expedited timeframes.
The internet is our primary critical business transaction channel. Internet availability
remains at risk due to geopolitical tensions and conflict.
Disruption to our IT systems and/or the internet (including breaches
of data security or cybersecurity, failure to integrate new and existing
IT systems) or failure to comply with additional requirements under
applicable laws, could harm our reputation and materially adversely
affect our financial condition or operations. While we invest heavily
in the protection of our data, IT, Operational Technology and AI
assets we may be unable to prevent hardware or software failures
or breaches which could result in disclosure of confidential
information, damage to our reputation, regulatory penalties
or sanctions, or financial loss.
The inability to back-up and restore data effectively could lead
to permanent loss of data that could, in turn, result in non-
compliance with applicable laws and regulations and otherwise harm
our business. Data loss could lead to public disclosure of confidential
information which may damage our reputation, materially affect our
business or results of operations, and expose us to legal risks and/or
additional legal obligations. Public disclosure of sensitive information
could materially adversely affect our reputation and business or
operations’ results.
Cybersecurity insurance coverage limits may not protect against
any future claim or claim proceeds may be delayed.
Failure to comply with regulatory disclosure requirements could
cause reputational damage and a loss of public trust.

rows.Enduring Risk: Failure to collect and manage data or AI in line with legal and regulatory requirements and strategic objectives
rows.Risk Statement: There is an increasing range of legislative and regulatory requirements to manage data across all countries where we conduct business such as restricting the movement of data between countries or how we make use of new technological capabilities such as AI. Failure to protect data effectively or the inappropriate use of technologies such as AI may lead to competitive disadvantage and/or loss of trust from key stakeholders, including patients, and prevent us from reaching our strategic objectives. In addition, failure to identify, prioritise and scale the appropriate AI opportunities may limit our ability to realise the benefits of AI in support of our strategic objectives.
rows.Risk Category: Supply chain and business execution risks
rows.Current Year Update:
Data is increasingly recognised as being AstraZeneca’s most valuable commodity.
There is an increasing range of legislative and regulatory requirements to manage
data across all countries where we conduct business. The requirements may impact
certain types of data such as personal data, the way that we conduct business, such
as restricting the movement of data between countries or jurisdictional regions,
or how we make use of new technological capabilities such as AI. In addition,
geopolitical changes may require changes to how AstraZeneca manages data.
Beyond legal and regulatory requirements, achieving strategic objectives will require
good management of data across the enterprise. As our organisation increasingly
relies on data, including sensitive data relating to health and genomics, a failure to
properly understand personal and collective accountabilities for managing data to
maximise its value, or failure to address data risks, will reduce our ability to execute
at pace and deliver strategic objectives.
AI technologies present significant opportunities and risks to our business.
Harnessing AI’s transformative potential may enable AstraZeneca to speed up the
discovery and development of new drugs, optimise our manufacturing processes,
drive efficiencies and productivity, and accelerate our growth. Failure to exploit
these opportunities may put AstraZeneca at a competitive disadvantage and impact
delivery of our strategic objectives.
AstraZeneca is investing significant resources into AI experimentation, development
and deployment across many parts of our business. As we scale our use of AI, it is
possible not all investments will succeed.
AI technologies may exacerbate existing risks, like those risks associated with data
privacy, cybersecurity and IP. AI also introduces new risks due to the autonomous
nature of the technology, the ease at which AI-enabled decision making can be
scaled up, and the commercial pressures to adopt AI. AI systems can amplify biased
and discriminatory decision making, perform unreliably and malfunction, generate
insights which are difficult to interpret and explain, and cause direct harm to
individuals or groups. These risks may become more significant as we increasingly
utilise AI to inform, augment and automate decision making and processes in
sensitive areas (e.g. clinical trials and medical decision making).
The adoption and exploitation of AI is occurring under the backdrop of intense global
media scrutiny, heightened political attention and low levels of public trust and
understanding. There is also a range of new AI regulations being adopted and
implemented worldwide, including in the EU, China and the US.
Despite taking measures designed to ensure compliance with
applicable privacy- and AI-related laws and regulations by our
personnel and our third parties, non-compliance may occur. If future
instances of non-compliance are deemed significant, these may
attract material regulatory sanctions or fines and corresponding
reputational damage, orders to stop certain processing of personal
data, or legal action on behalf of impacted individuals. Further, failure
to protect personal data could lead to a competitive disadvantage,
loss of trust from our stakeholders, including patients, and prevent
us from delivering our strategic objectives.
If the scope of data-related laws is expanded or if the interpretation
or enforcement of existing laws change or new privacy laws are
implemented, AstraZeneca and its third-party vendors may be
required to change their business practices or data processing
practices and policies. This may lead to substantial compliance-
related costs or materially adversely impact our business and
financial condition.
Our failure to use AI technologies in a way that maintains trust,
quality and control in our business activities would pose reputational,
legal, regulatory and financial risks to AstraZeneca. Investments in
AI may not realise the benefits that were anticipated.

WHAT & WHY
The compliance programme (and the controls contained therein) provide the key mitigation for our compliance risks.  The Annual Review monitors the effectiveness of the programme as a whole and the specific controls therein and sets out any improvements that are needed.

HOW
There is an annual cycle of reporting from the Chief Compliance Officer to the Audit Committee on the following areas of internal control:    
- Adequacy of the AZ Ethics Helpline (AZ Ethics point);                                                                                                             
 -  Monitoring and review of the effectiveness of our anti-bribery and anti-corruption controls        
- Review of the Code of Ethics (and related policies);                                                                                                                                                                                                 
-  Service assurance of the implementation and operation of the Code of Ethics;                 
- review the Company’s procedures for detecting fraud                                                                                                                      
- Review of the scope for compliance effectiveness reviews and review of the resources for, the role, effectiveness, structure and organisation of the compliance function.  (IRM:  CTRL0032451 and CTRL0032454)

WHEN
Annual cycle of reporting

Material Controls.Name: Data Enablement Council
Material Controls.Description:
WHAT & WHY
Data controls are required to ensure that data is of high quality and is being managed appropriately.  Review is also required to ensure that legislation (including that relating to AI) understood and being complied with.

HOW
As part of the organization's commitment to robust governance and risk management, an Enterprise Data Council (EDC) has been established; along with supporting governance meetings including SEDO forum, Data Assurance Board and the AI Assurance Board, to review and triage risks and issues presented to EDC.   The EDC review the following:
•	Effectiveness of Data and AI Controls: Assessment of the design, implementation, and ongoing effectiveness of the organization’s data and AI controls.
•	Assurance:  Summary of findings from assurance providers.
•	Incidents: Summary of significant incidents, including actions taken and lessons learned.
•	Emerging Risks: Identification of emerging risks and their potential implications for the organization.
•	Function Review: Evaluation of the structure and resources for managing data risks.
The EDC also opine on whether the controls in place manage the data and AI risks to an acceptable level.  
For any identified gaps or areas requiring improvement, remediation plans, along with timelines for resolution, are agreed. The EDC are also provided with updates on progress against previously established remediation plans to ensure accountability and continuous improvement.
The Chair of the EDC summarises the above in a report that is shared with the Audit Committee.

TBC

rows.Enduring Risk: Geopolitical and / or macroeconomic volatility disrupts operation of our global business
rows.Risk Statement: With an active presence in more than 80 countries, we are subject to political, socio-economic and financial factors around the world. A sustained global economic downturn or significant changes to exchange rates may adversely impact our business. Geopolitical tensions may lead to the imposition, alteration or escalation of trade controls, tariffs, taxes or other restrictions to market access, which may increase our costs or reduce revenues.
rows.Current Year Update:
With an active presence in more than 80 countries, we are subject to political,
socio-economic and financial factors around the world. A sustained global economic
downturn, periods of high inflation, stagflation or large fluctuation in exchange rates
may adversely impact financial markets and/or exacerbate pressure from
governments and other healthcare payers on medicine prices and other cost
control measures in order to limit healthcare spending.
Geopolitical tensions may lead to the imposition, alteration or escalation of trade
controls, tariffs, taxes or other restrictions to market access which may increase
our costs or reduce revenues.
A severe or prolonged economic downturn could result in a variety
of risks to our business, including weakened demand for medicines
and our ability to raise additional capital when needed or on
favourable terms, if at all. A weak or declining economy could strain
our suppliers, possibly resulting in supply disruption, or cause
delays in payments for our services by third-party payers.
Measures taken to limit healthcare spending may lead to lower than
anticipated rates of growth in some markets and limit the incentives
to develop innovative medicines, resulting in an adverse impact
on revenues and profitability.
Any escalation in barriers to the global free flow of medicines could
increase costs to serve affected markets which may lead to
downward pressure on margins. While the introduction of severe
sanctions would be unprecedented in relation to medicines, the
landscape continues to evolve. It could occur if matters escalate

rows.Enduring Risk: IP risks related to our products
rows.Risk Statement: The pharmaceutical industry is experiencing pressure from governments and other payers to impose limits on IP protections to manage healthcare costs. If we are unable to obtain, defend and enforce our IP, we may experience accelerated and intensified competition.
rows.Current Year Update:
IP protection provides the foundation for continued investment in developing
innovative medicines to improve patient health. However, the pharmaceutical
industry is experiencing pressure from governments and other healthcare payers to
impose limits on IP protections in an effort to manage healthcare costs. Additionally,
policymakers are progressively leveraging regulations to expedite the approval of
generic drugs and encourage generic drug utilisation. These policies may drive
accelerated utilisation of generic alternatives to our products following expiry
or loss of our IP rights. We also recognise increasing use of compulsory licensing
in some countries in which we operate.
We are subject to numerous patent challenges relating to various products or
processes and assertions of non-infringement of our patents. A loss in any of these
challenges could result in loss of patent protection on the covered product and a risk
to the revenue generated by the product. We also face the risk that our products may
be found to infringe patents owned or licensed by third parties and we may be
subject to monetary damages or compelled to cease sales of the infringing product,
resulting in a potential risk to revenue. These challenges threaten the value of our
investment in pharmaceutical development.
If we are unable to obtain, defend and enforce our IP, we may
experience accelerated and intensified competition. Also, if our
products are found to infringe a third-party patent, we may be
subject to monetary damages or compelled to cease sales of the
infringing product. These negative outcomes could have an adverse
material impact on our financial results.

Material Controls.Name: Patent filing, docketing and enforcement
Material Controls.Description:
WHAT & WHY
Intellectual property protection is critical to AstraZeneca’s business model. Each year, AstraZeneca invests billions of dollars into the research and development of innovative medicines and it often takes over 10 years of investment from initial discovery of a potential drug through clinical testing and commercialization. Without adequate patent protection, generic and biosimilar companies could copy and compete with AstraZeneca soon after drug approval by the FDA/EMA or the equivalent foreign regulatory agency. Given the size and complexity of AstraZeneca’s business, it is important to have internal controls which exist to ensure appropriate intellectual property protection is obtained and maintained throughout their lifecycle for material products in key markets, and that “freedom to operate” is assessed prior to commercialization.

HOW
AstraZeneca’s Global Intellectual Property (GIP) group is accountable for obtaining patent protection for each novel medicine composition of matter (COM) prior to initiation of human clinical trials. Typically, the initial patent applications are filed at the time the Candidate Drug (CD) is approved by the Early Stage Product Committee (ESPC). The number of countries where a patent application is filed is pre-determined by the IP Leadership Team (IPLT). The list is updated by IPLT in collaboration with the appropriate Commercial organization no later than every three years for material products in key markets. The IPLT, organized by therapy area, monitors and assures compliance with control IP001. Each filing is also reviewed by the Quality Enhancement (QE) team (a subgroup of GIP patent attorneys) and the relevant inventors, and the QE team keeps track of COM CD cases reviewed. All deadline-driven activities relating to material COM filings, e.g., annuity due dates, and other substantive correspondence with patent offices around the world are saved and “docketed” in GIP’s document management (iManage) and docketing systems (Anaqua). IPLT is accountable for ensuring Control IP004 is met. IP Operations conducts a monthly review of docketed activities and maintenance requirements and sends this to the SVP IP.

WHEN
Event driven (prior to human clinical trials[ for material COM filings], annuity due dates)

Material Controls.Description:
WHAT & WHY

HOW
The Patent Health Check involves assessment of both the scope of patent protection and freedom to operate with respect to the pipeline molecule COM in question.   No later than Phase 3 material investment decision (Phase 3 ID) of a new chemical entity (NCE), which is approved by the Late-Stage Product Committee (LSPC), an assigned patent attorney from GIP performs a “Patent Health Check.”  The Patent Health Check involves assessment of both the scope of patent protection and freedom to operate with respect to the pipeline molecule composition of matter (COM) in question.   Results of the Patent Health Check are communicated to the SVP IP, the IPLT member for the relevant therapy area and the Global Product Team Leader (GPT-L).  The conclusions and analysis are further captured in a written memo to the SVP IP and risk mitigation steps are actioned as necessary.   IPLT is accountable for ensuring that Control IP002 is met.

Material Controls.Name: Review of litigation matters
Material Controls.Description:
WHAT & WHY
Legal proceedings need to be disclosed to ensure investors are provided with clear and balanced information about the company. (in line with listing requirements)

HOW
Each quarter, a member of B&CS sends an e-mail to each member of the LSMT (excluding the Company Secretary) asking them to disclose any known material litigation and to review the Legal Proceedings note disclosed in the quarterly results announcements and to consider:
(i) whether any material developments have occurred that require those disclosures to be updated; and
(ii) whether there are any material developments in the previously disclosed Legal Proceedings note (including threatened and/or pending legal proceedings) and/or new legal proceedings (including threatened and/or pending legal proceedings) which may require to be disclosed in the Legal Proceedings note disclosed in the quarterly results announcements. Material developments are changes that would cause an investor to alter their forecasts.

All responses from the LSMT are to be collected prior to the GFR lock meeting that precedes approval of the final quarterly results announcement and are held on file. A member of B&CS under supervision of the Deputy Company Secretary or the Company Secretary ensures that all changes identified in this process are considered for inclusion the Legal Proceedings note.
In the event that any LSMT member fails to provide a response, the Deputy Company Secretary or the General Counsel may confirm their approval of the disclosures to satisfy the control. Any such confirmations are to be noted in writing (including email) and held on file.

Notice of material litigations occur by either in-person, email, or mail service to AZ central offices and are sent to the accountable member of the Legal Senior Management Team.  On a quarterly basis, a list of pending litigation matters from Counsellink is sent to all case managers and email confirmation is required to ensure that there are no pending material (against a materiality threshold of US $100m) litigation matters that do not appear on this list. 

An internal legal and risk meeting is held (between Legal and Finance) to discuss open material litigation and any developments that may or may not require a provision to be established. Discussions are held through the quarter relating to the accounting considerations.  A formal meeting is then conducted at the quarter end.  Minutes are taken and approved under the Accounting issues control.  (This is part of GFR C36 controls).

In addition, the litigation disclosures are set out in a separate Legal Log by a member of Legal under supervision of the Deputy General Counsel (the Legal Log). The Legal Log includes legal entity information and accounting treatment for each legal matter, detailing which matters are disclosed for the purposes of contingent liabilities, provisions and contingent assets. Each quarter the Legal Log is sent by the Deputy General Counsel to the Head of Technical Accounting Compliance & UK Reporting for review. Once agreed by the Head of Technical Accounting Compliance & UK Reporting and the Deputy General Counsel, the Legal Log confirms the final accounting position for each legal matter disclosed in the Legal Proceedings note for the quarter.

Prior to the GFR lock meeting that precedes approval of the final quarterly results announcement, the Head of Technical Accounting Compliance & UK Reporting confirms to the Deputy Company Secretary that the Legal Log has been updated and agreed between the Head of Technical Accounting Compliance & UK Reporting and the Deputy General Counsel and that the agreed accounting positions are reflected in the quarterly results announcement. 

WHEN
Quarterly

Material Controls.Name: Accounting issues
Material Controls.Description:
WHAT & WHY
Quarterly Accounting Issue meetings are held with FSMT VP's (or delegate) and significant business function key finance staff (VP or delegate) to ensure that GFR is informed of all significant accounting issues, with the exception of deals which are confirmed with Deal Finance and the SVP GPPM, Strategic Planning and Business Development. GFR then review the quarterly ERH submission to ensure all reported matters deemed significant (generally new, unusual and above $20m) are included in the quarterly reported numbers. The purpose of this control is to ensure that the quarterly, half year and annual financial statements reflect all significant accounting matters and such matters are appropriately recorded in the books and records of the AZ Group.

HOW
SET area Accounting Issues summary documents are provided by the SET areas, and provided to GFR, or emails detailing the issues raised are sent and agreement by the appropriate contact is obtained.

Confirmations are filed on the quarter end SOX file and evidence of completeness of receipt of minutes and appropriate SET area sign off. A quarterly summary of Group issues is prepared by the GFR Head of Technical Accounting & Compliance based on the confirmations received, and other accounting issues notifications and discussions in the quarter. Evidence of review of the minutes for evidence of matters being considered for inclusion in the quarterly summary document is included in the quarter end SOX file.

The quarterly summary is reviewed with the SVP Finance Group Controller (or delegate), and VP Finance, Group Financial Reporting (or delegate), who confirm their agreement with the summary (meeting normally WD -1).

Completeness and accuracy of the SET area accounting issues minutes are confirmed by the FSMT VP's (or in exceptional circumstances, delegate) prior to final Working Day 8 lock, with the exception of deals which are confirmed by the SVP GPPM, Strategic Planning and Business Development. Any outstanding FSMT confirmations are noted in the work day 8 lock meeting and followed up in the final pre-announcement lock meeting to make sure confirmation have been received.

The accounting issues identified in the quarterly summary are reviewed by the statement accountants against the financial statements used for the full lock meeting to ensure all are dealt with appropriately in those statements.

WHEN
Quarterly

Material Controls.Name: Subsequent events
Material Controls.Description:
WHAT & WHY
The subsequent event returns are collated by the Consolidation accountants who obtain returns from FSMT/SET area VP's or equivalent/delegate to populate the Subsequent Events Control Sheet on a quarterly basis.  This is then reviewed by the VP of Group Reporting or delegate (Head of Technical Accounting and Compliance or the Head of Technical Accounting and Group Consolidation) and reflected, as appropriate, in the financial statements.  The purpose of this control is to ensure that any significant items with an accounting impact of $10m that have arisen post lock meeting are considered and concluded on as adjusting or non-adjusting events and for disclosure purposes.

HOW
i) Email confirmations are collated from all SET areas prior to final lock meeting, requesting information on any events that have arisen post Lock meeting
ii) The VP of Group Reporting checks all confirmations have been received, and the items contained in the confirmations are appropriately included in the Subsequent Events Control Sheet.
iii) The results are assessed un the criteria contained within IAS10, as to whether they are considered adjusting or non-adjusting, and whether disclosure is required, both individually and in aggregate and are discussed and minuted at pre-announcement lock meeting.
iv) Evidence of this review is documented on the Subsequent Events Control Sheet.  Any appropriate events are considered at the pre-announcement lock meeting, this review is document in the pre-announcement lock meeting minutes.

WHEN
